subject: Ephemeral key handling & retention - MediWave POC
messages:
From: Anna Patel <anna@mediwave.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Ephemeral key handling & retention - MediWave POC

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. MediWave is ready to move the POC into our internal security review but we have a couple of specific asks before we can sign off on the onboarding timeline:

1) Evidence: sample audit logs that show key usage at the per-request level (timestamps, requester id, model endpoint, key-id).
2) Ephemeral keys: confirmation of how ephemeral keys are generated/rotated for short-lived sessions, and any guarantees about cache eviction/kv persistence.
3) BYOK/KMS options: we need to know what you can support for a POC (customer-managed KMS vs ephemeral proxy keys), and whether key material ever leaves the customer-controlled boundary.
4) Retention: default retention windows for token logs and request traces and whether we can request shorter retention for POC data.

I've attached our compliance checklist (MediWave_Compliance_Checklist.xlsx). Can you point me to a short playbook or a single page summary we can hand to our security team? Also would like a rough timeline for the evidence we can provide — ideally within 3 business days.

Anna
Anna Patel
Head of Product Security, MediWave
ops+security@mediwave.com

Attachments: MediWave_Compliance_Checklist.xlsx
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Ephemeral key handling & retention - MediWave POC

Anna — thanks for sending this over and for the clear checklist. I copied Security (Irene), Product (Marissa) and Ops (Ben) so we can triage the asks quickly. First pass below; will follow up with a short triage doc and an action timeline.

Quick answers up front:
- Audit logs: we can provide a sample slice of request traces (no user PII) showing key-id, timestamp, endpoint and request metadata.
- Ephemeral keys: we support an ephemeral proxy key for POCs (short-lived, rotated hourly) and a BYOK path (customer-managed KMS) for Dedicated/Private deployments. Ephemeral proxy keys do not persist key material to long-term storage; they are cached in-memory on inference nodes and rotated/evicted according to TTL.
- BYOK/KMS: for the POC we can run a proof-mode where you hold key material in your KMS and we call it via a secure proxy; this does not export raw key material to Redwood.
- Retention: default request trace retention is 90 days on hosted; for POC we can propose a 7–30 day short retention window for the MediWave tenant.

Action items (triage plan):
1) Security will produce a 1-page evidence pack (audit log sample + explanation of key flows).
2) Product will scope any UI/API config we need to toggle short-retention for the tenant.
3) Ops will generate an ephemeral-playbook draft that describes rotation policy, TTLs, and eviction guarantees.

Irene/Marissa/Ben — can you each confirm feasibility and owners for the items above? Anna, I'll send the triage doc and a calendar invite for a 30-min sync this afternoon if that works.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-ephemeral-playbook-draft.md (draft)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Ephemeral key handling & retention - MediWave POC

Michael / Anna — adding technical detail for the evidence pack and a few constraints so expectations are aligned.

What we can provide quickly:
- A redacted sample of audit entries (JSON lines) for a 48-hour window showing: timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, model, token_count, key_id (redacted format: key-xxxxx), region, and request latency. No customer payload included.
- A diagram and short write-up describing ephemeral key lifecycle for POCs: generation at bootstrap, hourly rotation, in-memory KV cache on the serving node, eviction on node restart, and explicit revoke API.

Important caveats:
- Ephemeral proxy keys are derived from a root that is managed by Redwood in hosted mode; the derivation is one-way and raw root material is not accessible to customer. If you require full customer control over root key material, you must run Dedicated or Private with BYOK integrated to your KMS.
- TTL semantics: we guarantee rotation every hour and eviction within 5 minutes of TTL expiry; however, there may be a short tail where cached KV entries persist for ongoing sessions (we will document the maximum window).

Temporary mitigations we can offer for the POC:
- Short retention flag at the tenant level (7–30 days) — Product to confirm UI/API timeline.
- Escrow path: we can create an encrypted escrow of key references that MediWave can request for audit, with access logs. This is not an export of key material.

Related work & references:
- Jira: SEC-4821 (ephemeral key lifecycle improvements)
- Internal KB: kb-ephemeral-keys.pdf (attached)

I can assemble the redacted audit sample and the short playbook this afternoon. Michael — if Ops can confirm the exact TTL tail number I can include it in the write-up.

Irene Choi
Director, Security Engineering — Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

I'll attach the audit slice and the playbook to the calendar invite Michael is sending. Planning to mark owners in the doc: Irene (security write-up), Marissa (short-retention flag scope), Ben (ops evidence + appendix).
